text: Which of these best defines the World Wide Web?
options: A physical network of cables connecting computers
A system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet
A single website containing all information
explanation: The World Wide Web (WWW) is a system of interlinked hypertext documents (web pages) that are accessed over the Internet using a web browser.

text: A computer that stores web pages and delivers them to browsers on request is called a
explanation: A web server is a computer that stores website files and responds to requests from web clients (browsers) by sending the requested pages.

text: Which software is used by a user to view and interact with web pages?
explanation: A web browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox) is client-side software used to request pages from a web server and display them to the user.

text: A regularly updated personal website featuring commentary or journal-style entries is called a
explanation: A blog (short for weblog) is a personal or informational website displaying entries in reverse chronological order, usually maintained by an individual or small group.

text: An online discussion group where people post messages on a shared topic is known as a
explanation: A newsgroup is an online discussion forum where users post and read messages on a specific topic of common interest.

text: The language most commonly used to create web pages is
explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language used to create the structure and content of web pages.

text: In the web address https://www.cbse.gov.in, which part identifies the top-level domain?
explanation: The top-level domain (TLD) is the last segment of the domain name; here '.in' indicates the country-code TLD for India (with .gov being a second-level domain indicating a government site).

text: An e-mail address such as student@school.edu.in is divided into a username and a
explanation: An e-mail address has the format username@domainname, where the part after '@' is the domain name of the mail server handling that account.

text: Transferring a file from a remote server to your own computer is called
explanation: Downloading refers to copying a file from a remote server to the local computer; the reverse process is called uploading.

text: Sending a file from your local computer to a remote server is called
explanation: Uploading is the process of transferring a file from a local computer to a remote server over a network.

text: Which protocol suite forms the basic communication language of the Internet?
explanation: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the fundamental set of protocols that governs how data is broken into packets, addressed, transmitted and reassembled across the Internet.

text: Which protocol is used to send outgoing e-mail from a client to a mail server?
explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending and relaying outgoing e-mail messages between mail servers and from a client to its outgoing server.

text: Which protocol is used by an e-mail client to retrieve and download messages from a mail server?
explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is used by e-mail clients to retrieve messages stored on a mail server, typically downloading them to the local device.

text: Which protocol governs the transfer of ordinary (unencrypted) web pages between a browser and a server?
explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) defines how requests and responses for web pages are exchanged between a browser and a web server, without encryption.

text: HTTPS differs from HTTP mainly because HTTPS
options: encrypts data using SSL/TLS for secure transmission
is used only for sending e-mail
does not require a web server
explanation: HTTPS (HTTP Secure) is HTTP layered with SSL/TLS encryption, so data exchanged between browser and server is encrypted and protected from eavesdropping.

text: Which protocol allows a user to securely log in to and execute commands on a remote computer over an encrypted connection?
explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) provides an encrypted channel for remote login and command execution, unlike TELNET which sends data, including passwords, in plain text.

text: Which protocol is used to transfer files securely over an SSH connection?
explanation: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) runs over SSH and encrypts both commands and data, providing a secure alternative to plain FTP.

text: Which of the following protocols transfers files between computers WITHOUT encrypting the data?
explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) transmits files and login credentials in plain text, making it insecure compared to SFTP or SCP, which use SSH-based encryption.

text: SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) is primarily used to
options: securely copy files between hosts over SSH
translate domain names to IP addresses
explanation: SCP allows secure copying of files between a local and a remote host, or between two remote hosts, using the SSH protocol for authentication and encryption.

text: TELNET is a protocol used for
options: remote login to another computer over a network
explanation: TELNET allows a user to log in to and operate a remote computer over a network, though it is considered insecure since data is sent unencrypted.

text: Which of the following is a program that helps users locate information on the Internet by keyword?
explanation: A search engine (e.g., Google, Bing) indexes web content and allows users to locate relevant sites and pages by entering keywords.

text: Real-time text communication between two or more users over the Internet is called
explanation: Chat is a web service that allows users to exchange text messages in real time over the Internet.

text: Conducting meetings between people at different locations using audio and video over the Internet is called
explanation: Video conferencing is an Internet-based service that allows participants at different locations to see and hear each other in real time for a meeting or discussion.

text: Delivering educational content and conducting classes over the Internet is known as
explanation: e-Learning refers to using the Internet and digital technology to deliver educational content, courses, and training to learners remotely.

text: Carrying out banking transactions such as fund transfer and bill payment over the Internet is called
explanation: e-Banking allows customers to perform banking transactions like balance enquiry, fund transfer, and bill payments through the Internet instead of visiting a branch.

text: Buying and selling goods and services through websites is known as
explanation: e-Shopping (online shopping) is the process of purchasing goods or services over the Internet through e-commerce websites.

text: Government services delivered to citizens electronically over the Internet, such as filing returns or applying for certificates online, are examples of
explanation: e-Governance refers to the use of the Internet and IT to deliver government information and services to citizens electronically.

text: An online mailing list where members subscribe to receive and share messages on a common topic is called
explanation: e-Groups (or online groups) are Internet-based mailing lists or communities where subscribed members share messages, files and discussions on a common interest.

text: Booking tickets for trains, flights or movies online is an example of which web service?
explanation: e-Reservation refers to booking services such as train, flight, or event tickets online through the Internet.

text: Which mobile technology is designed only for sending short text messages of limited length between mobile phones?
explanation: SMS (Short Message Service) allows the exchange of short text-only messages (traditionally up to 160 characters) between mobile phones.

text: Which tag is used to define the root element of an HTML document?
explanation: The <html> tag is the root element that encloses the entire HTML document, including the <head> and <body> sections.

text: Which HTML tag contains meta-information about the document such as its title, not displayed in the browser window?
explanation: The <head> tag holds information about the document (like <title>, <meta>, and links to style sheets) that is not directly displayed in the visible page content.

text: Which tag defines the text that appears on the browser's title bar or tab?
explanation: The <title> tag, placed inside <head>, specifies the text shown on the browser's title bar or tab for that page.

text: Which tag contains all the visible content of a web page, such as text and images?
explanation: The <body> tag contains all the content that is displayed to the user in the browser window, such as text, images, links and tables.

text: Which attribute of the <body> tag is used to set the background colour of a web page?
explanation: The bgcolor attribute of the <body> tag sets the background colour of the entire web page, e.g. <body bgcolor="yellow">.

text: Which attribute of the <body> tag is used to specify an image as the page background?
explanation: The background attribute of the <body> tag is used to set an image file as the background of the web page.

text: Which <body> attribute sets the default colour of hyperlinks that have not yet been visited?
explanation: The link attribute of <body> specifies the colour of unvisited hyperlinks on the page.

text: Which <body> attribute sets the colour of a link at the moment it is being clicked (activated)?
explanation: The alink attribute of <body> defines the colour a hyperlink takes on while it is actively being clicked.

text: Which <body> attribute sets the colour of hyperlinks that have already been visited?
explanation: The vlink attribute of <body> specifies the colour applied to hyperlinks that the user has previously visited.

text: Which tag is used to insert a single line break within text, without starting a new paragraph?
explanation:
The
tag inserts a line break, moving following content to a new line, and is an empty (self-closing) tag.

text: Which tag draws a horizontal line across the page, often used to separate sections?
explanation: The <hr> tag inserts a horizontal rule (a horizontal line) across the page, commonly used to visually separate content sections.

text: How are comments written in HTML source code so that they are ignored by the browser?
explanation: HTML comments are written between <!-- and -->; the browser ignores this text when rendering the page, but it remains visible in the source code.

text: Which tag pair represents the largest (most prominent) heading level in HTML?
explanation: HTML provides six heading levels, <h1> to <h6>; <h1> represents the largest and most important heading, while <h6> is the smallest.

text: Which tag is used to define a paragraph of text?
explanation:
The

tag defines a paragraph, and browsers automatically add space before and after it.

text: Which tag makes enclosed text appear in bold?
explanation: The <b> tag renders the enclosed text in bold typeface.

text: Which tag makes enclosed text appear italicised?
explanation: The <i> tag displays the enclosed text in italics.

text: Which tag underlines the enclosed text?
explanation: The <u> tag renders the enclosed text with an underline.

text: Which tag is used to create a bulleted (unordered) list?
explanation: The <ul> tag defines an unordered list, whose items are marked with bullets by default, with each item wrapped in an <li> tag.

text: Which tag is used to create a numbered (ordered) list?
explanation: The <ol> tag defines an ordered list whose items are automatically numbered, with each item wrapped in an <li> tag.

text: Which tag is used to define an individual item within an ordered or unordered list?
explanation: The <li> (list item) tag defines each entry within an <ol> or <ul> list.

text: In a description list, which tag encloses the entire list?
explanation: The <dl> tag defines a description list, which contains term-definition pairs marked using <dt> (term) and <dd> (description).

text: In a description list, which tag is used to specify the description/definition of a term?
explanation: The <dd> tag is used inside a <dl> to provide the description or definition corresponding to the preceding <dt> term.

text: Which attribute of the <ol> tag is used to change the starting number of the list?
explanation: The start attribute of <ol> specifies the number (or letter/roman numeral position) at which the ordered list should begin counting, e.g. <ol start="5">.

text: Which attribute of <ol> or <ul> is used to change the numbering style (e.g., to Roman numerals or letters) or bullet style of a list?
explanation: The type attribute of <ol> sets the numbering style (1, A, a, I, i) and the type attribute of <ul> sets the bullet style (disc, circle, square).

text: Which attribute of the <font> tag is used to change the typeface of text, such as Arial or Times New Roman?
explanation: The face attribute of the <font> tag specifies the typeface/font family to be used for the enclosed text, e.g. <font face="Arial">.

text: Which attribute of the <font> tag controls the size of the displayed text?
explanation: The size attribute of the <font> tag sets the size of the text, typically using values from 1 (smallest) to 7 (largest).

text: Which attribute of the tag specifies the path or URL of the image file to be displayed?
explanation: The src attribute of the tag specifies the source location (path or URL) of the image file to be embedded in the page.

text: Which attribute of the tag provides alternative text shown if the image cannot be displayed?
explanation: The alt attribute provides alternate descriptive text for an image, which is displayed if the image fails to load and is also used by screen readers.

text: Which tag displays text raised slightly above the normal line, such as in x2 written as a power?
explanation: The <sup> tag renders enclosed text as superscript, raised above the baseline, commonly used for exponents like x<sup>2</sup>.

text: Which tag displays text lowered slightly below the normal line, such as the '2' in H2O?
explanation: The <sub> tag renders enclosed text as subscript, positioned below the baseline, commonly used for chemical formulas like H<sub>2</sub>O.

text: Which HTML form input type is used to accept a single line of visible text from the user, such as a name?
explanation: <input type="text"> creates a single-line text box in which the user can type and see visible characters, such as a name field.

text: Which HTML form input type masks the characters typed by the user, showing dots or asterisks instead?
explanation: <input type="password"> creates a text field where typed characters are masked (shown as dots/asterisks) for confidentiality, such as for login passwords.

text: Which HTML form element allows a user to select only ONE option from a set of mutually exclusive choices?
explanation: Radio buttons (<input type="radio">) are grouped using the same name attribute and allow the user to select only one option from the group at a time.

text: Which HTML form element allows a user to select MULTIPLE independent options, each of which can be ticked on or off?
explanation: Checkboxes (<input type="checkbox">) allow the user to select zero, one, or more options independently, unlike radio buttons which allow only one from a group.

text: Which tag creates a drop-down list (combo box) in an HTML form, from which a user picks one option?
explanation: The <select> tag creates a drop-down list/combo box in a form, with each choice defined using an <option> tag nested inside it.

text: The set of accepted rules of polite and responsible behaviour while communicating on the Internet is called
explanation: Netiquette (network + etiquette) refers to the accepted rules of polite, respectful and responsible online behaviour, such as not spamming or using offensive language.

text: A type of software license that allows users to freely use, study, modify and distribute the source code is called
explanation: An open source software license grants users the right to freely access, use, study, modify and redistribute the program's source code, subject to certain conditions.

text: Software that is fully copyrighted and whose source code is kept private by the owning company is called
explanation: Proprietary software is owned and controlled by a company or individual; its source code is not made public, and usage is restricted by licensing terms.

text: Software that can be used free of cost but whose source code is not necessarily made available is called
explanation: Freeware is software that is distributed and can be used at no cost, but unlike open source software, its source code may not be publicly available for modification.

text: Software distributed on a trial basis, often with limited features or a time limit, after which the user must pay to continue using it, is called
explanation: Shareware is software provided free for a trial period or with restricted features, requiring payment to unlock full functionality or continue use afterward.

text: The legal rights given to creators over their original creations of the mind, such as inventions, literary works and designs, are collectively known as
explanation: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) are legal rights that protect creations of the mind, such as inventions, literary and artistic works, symbols and designs, giving creators control over their use.

text: Presenting someone else's work, words or ideas as one's own without giving proper credit is called
explanation: Plagiarism is the act of using another person's work, ideas or words without proper acknowledgment and presenting them as one's own, which is considered an ethical and academic offence.

text: The exclusive legal right granted to the creator of an original work (like a book, song or software) to control its use and distribution is called
explanation: Copyright is a legal right that grants the creator of an original literary, artistic or software work exclusive control over its reproduction, distribution and use.

text: A distinctive sign, symbol or logo used to identify a company's products and distinguish them from others is protected under a
explanation: A trademark is a recognizable sign, symbol, logo or name legally registered to identify and distinguish a company's goods or services from those of others.

text: An exclusive right granted for a new invention, preventing others from making, using or selling it without permission for a set period, is called a
explanation: A patent grants an inventor exclusive rights to their invention for a limited period, preventing others from manufacturing, using or selling it without authorisation.

text: The unequal access that different groups of people have to digital technology and the Internet, often due to economic or geographic reasons, is called the
explanation: The digital divide refers to the gap between individuals or communities who have adequate access to computers and the Internet and those who do not, often due to economic, social or geographic factors.

text: The principle that citizens have the right to access information held by public authorities and government bodies is known as
explanation: Freedom of information refers to the right of citizens to access information held by government and public authorities, promoting transparency and accountability.

text: In e-commerce, the protection of a customer's personal and financial data from being seen or misused by unauthorised parties is referred to as
explanation: Privacy in e-commerce refers to protecting a customer's personal and financial information from unauthorised access, disclosure or misuse during online transactions.

text: Deceptive activities intended to illegally obtain money or sensitive information from victims during online transactions are collectively called
explanation: E-commerce fraud refers to deceptive or dishonest practices, such as fake websites or phishing, aimed at illegally obtaining money, goods or sensitive information from online shoppers.

text: Encrypting data before sending it over the Internet, such as using HTTPS during an online purchase, ensures which of the following in e-commerce?
explanation: Secure data transmission uses encryption protocols (like SSL/TLS in HTTPS) to protect data, such as payment details, as it travels between the customer's browser and the e-commerce server, preventing interception.

text: In Scratch, the visual objects that can be programmed to move and interact are called:
explanation: Sprites are the on-screen objects/characters in Scratch that are controlled by stacking blocks of code.

text: Which category of Scratch blocks would you use to make a sprite say something in a speech bubble?
explanation: The 'Looks' block category contains blocks like 'say' and 'think' that display speech/thought bubbles above a sprite.

text: Which Scratch block category contains 'move 10 steps' and 'turn 15 degrees'?
explanation: The Motion category controls a sprite's position and direction, including 'move' and 'turn' blocks.

text: In Scratch, which block is used to start a script when the green flag is clicked?
explanation: 'when green flag clicked' is an Events block that triggers a script as soon as the user clicks the green flag to start the project.

text: Which Scratch block category is used to send a message that other sprites can react to?
explanation: 'Broadcast' and 'when I receive' blocks (found in Events) allow one sprite to send a message that triggers scripts in other sprites.

text: Which Scratch construct repeats a set of blocks continuously for as long as the program runs?
explanation: The 'forever' loop (Control category) repeats the enclosed blocks endlessly until the program is stopped.

text: In Scratch, which block category would you use to check 'is the sprite touching the edge?'
explanation: Sensing blocks let a sprite detect its environment, such as 'touching edge?', 'touching mouse-pointer?', and 'key pressed?'.

text: Which Scratch block would you use to store and update a score during a game?
explanation: Variables store changeable data such as score, lives, or time, and can be shown on the stage and updated with 'change [score] by 1' blocks.

text: In Scratch, what is the key difference between 'repeat 10' and 'repeat until <condition>'?
options: 'repeat 10' runs a fixed number of times; 'repeat until' runs until a condition becomes true
explanation: 'repeat 10' is a counted loop that always executes 10 times, while 'repeat until <condition>' keeps looping until the given condition evaluates to true — the number of iterations is not fixed in advance.

text: A different appearance/image a sprite can switch between (e.g. to animate walking) is called a:
explanation: A costume is one of the visual appearances a sprite can take; switching costumes rapidly creates the illusion of animation (e.g. walking).

text: Which Python function is used to display output on the screen?
explanation: print() outputs text or values to the console/screen. input() is used to read user input, not display output.

text: Which of the following is a valid Python variable name?
explanation: Python variable names can contain letters, digits, and underscores but cannot start with a digit or contain hyphens; 'class' is a reserved keyword so it cannot be used as a variable name.

text: Which Python data type would you use to store the value True or False?
explanation: The bool (Boolean) data type stores one of two values: True or False, commonly used in conditional logic.

text:
What will the following Python code print?
x = 5
y = 2
print(x // y)
explanation: The // operator performs integer (floor) division in Python, discarding the remainder: 5 // 2 = 2.

text: Which Python statement is used to take input from the user and store it as a string?
explanation: input() displays the prompt, waits for the user to type, and returns the entered text as a string, which is then assigned to the variable.

text: Which loop in Python is best suited to iterate a fixed number of times using range()?
explanation: Python's for loop combined with range() is the standard way to iterate a known, fixed number of times, e.g. for i in range(5):.

text: What is the correct Python syntax to check if a number stored in 'n' is even?
explanation: The modulus operator % gives the remainder of division; if n % 2 equals 0, the number n has no remainder when divided by 2, meaning it is even.

text:
What does the following Python code print?
total = 0
for i in range(1, 4):
    total = total + i
print(total)
explanation: range(1,4) generates 1, 2, 3. The loop adds each to total: 0+1=1, 1+2=3, 3+3=6. Final printed value is 6.

text: In Python, which keyword is used to define a reusable block of code (a function)?
explanation: Python uses the 'def' keyword to define a function, e.g. def greet(): followed by an indented code block.

text: Both Scratch and Python support which fundamental programming concept, used to make decisions based on a condition?
explanation: Selection (conditional branching using if-else) is a fundamental programming concept present in both Scratch (via 'if...then...else' blocks) and Python (via if-elif-else statements).

text: Suhani asks her colleague for her project work and then copies the entire work and submits it to her team leader claiming it to be her own work. The act performed by Suhani is known as ___.
explanation: Plagiarism is the act of taking someone else's work or ideas and presenting them as your own without giving proper credit. Suhani copied her colleague's project and submitted it as her own — that is plagiarism.

whyOthersWrong.a: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive information (passwords, credit card numbers) by disguising as a trustworthy entity. Suhani did not deceive anyone to obtain credentials.
whyOthersWrong.c: Spamming is sending unsolicited bulk messages. Suhani is copying intellectual work, not sending bulk messages.
whyOthersWrong.d: A virus is a malicious program that replicates and damages systems. Suhani's act involves copying work, not creating/spreading malware.

text: Which of the following is the correct expansion of SMS?
explanation: SMS stands for Short Message Service — it is the standard protocol for sending short text messages (up to 160 characters) over cellular networks.

whyOthersWrong.a: The S in SMS stands for 'Short', not 'Small'. Messages are 'short' in length, not 'small'.
whyOthersWrong.b: Both words are wrong: it is 'Short' not 'Small', and 'Message' not 'Multimedia'. Multimedia messaging uses MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service).
whyOthersWrong.c: The second word is wrong: SMS is 'Message' Service, not 'Multimedia' Service. Multimedia messaging is MMS.

text: Which of the following is an e-Shopping portal?
explanation: Flipkart is an Indian e-commerce platform where users can browse and purchase products online — it is an e-Shopping portal.

whyOthersWrong.a: Diksha (DIKSHA) is a national digital platform for school education launched by NCERT. It is an e-Learning portal, not e-Shopping.
whyOthersWrong.b: Swayam is a MOOC (Massive Open Online Course) platform by the Government of India for higher education. It is an e-Learning portal.
whyOthersWrong.d: NPTEL (National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning) is an online education portal by IITs and IISc. It is an e-Learning portal.

text: Which of the following is NOT an e-Governance portal?
explanation: Zomato is a food delivery and restaurant discovery application — it is a commercial service, not an e-Governance portal. All the others are government digital service portals.

whyOthersWrong.a: e-Aadhaar is the official online portal to download the digital copy of the Aadhaar card — it is an e-Governance service.
whyOthersWrong.b: DigiLocker is a Government of India initiative to provide a digital document wallet for citizens to store official documents — it is an e-Governance service.
whyOthersWrong.c: Sarathi (Parivahan Sarathi) is a government portal for driving licence-related services — it is an e-Governance service.

text: The protocol that is used to send e-mails is ___.
explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the standard protocol used for sending e-mails from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.

whyOthersWrong.a: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is used for transferring web pages on the World Wide Web, not for sending e-mails.
whyOthersWrong.b: POP (Post Office Protocol) is used for receiving/downloading e-mails from a mail server to a client. It is for receiving, not sending.
whyOthersWrong.d: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used for transferring files between a client and a server over a network. It is not used for e-mail.

text: SFTP is used for:

options.a: Sending Files over the Internet in a secure manner
options.b: Sending Mail over the Internet in a secure manner

explanation: SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) is a secure version of FTP that uses SSH encryption to transfer files over the Internet safely, protecting data from interception.

whyOthersWrong.b: Sending e-mail securely uses SMTPS or STARTTLS extensions. SFTP stands for Secure File Transfer Protocol and deals with files, not mail.
whyOthersWrong.c: Video conferencing uses protocols like H.323, SIP, or WebRTC — not SFTP. SFTP is purely for file transfers.
whyOthersWrong.d: Secure chat services use protocols such as XMPP with TLS or Signal Protocol. SFTP is not related to chat communication.

text: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of tag in HTML?
explanation: The tag does not have a 'color' attribute. Color styling is applied via CSS (color property applies to text, not images). Valid attributes include src, width, height, alt, align, border, etc.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'source' is a valid attribute of (though the standard spelling is 'src', 'source' refers to the same concept and is listed as an option here — the question asks specifically about 'color' being invalid).
whyOthersWrong.b: 'width' is a valid attribute of the tag used to specify the width of the image in pixels or percentage.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'alt' is a valid and important attribute of the tag used to provide alternative text for the image when it cannot be displayed.

text: HTML provides us with ___ levels of headings that can be inserted in a web page.
explanation: HTML provides 6 levels of headings: <h1> (largest/most important) through <h6> (smallest/least important). There is no <h7> or beyond in standard HTML.

whyOthersWrong.a: HTML has 6 heading levels (<h1> to <h6>), not 5. Choosing 5 would exclude <h6>.
whyOthersWrong.c: HTML does not have a <h7> tag. The standard stops at <h6>. There are exactly 6 heading levels.
whyOthersWrong.d: HTML does not have <h7> or <h8> tags. The standard defines exactly 6 heading levels (<h1> to <h6>).

text: Which of the following options is an INVALID attribute of <font> tag in HTML?
explanation: The <font> tag in HTML has three valid attributes: face (font family/typeface), size (font size 1–7), and color (text color). 'width' is not an attribute of the <font> tag; it is used for elements like tables, images, etc.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'face' is a valid attribute of the <font> tag that specifies the font family/typeface (e.g., <font face="Arial">).
whyOthersWrong.c: 'size' is a valid attribute of the <font> tag that specifies the font size on a scale of 1 to 7 (e.g., <font size="4">).
whyOthersWrong.d: 'color' is a valid attribute of the <font> tag that specifies the text color (e.g., <font color="red">).

text: The default starting value for an ordered list in HTML is ___.
explanation: By default, an HTML ordered list (<ol>) starts numbering from 1 (Arabic numerals). You can change the starting value using the 'start' attribute (e.g., <ol start="5">).

whyOthersWrong.a: 'i' is used for lowercase Roman numerals in ordered lists (type="i"), but it is not the default. The default type is Arabic numerals starting at 1.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'a' is used for lowercase alphabetical ordered lists (type="a"), but it is not the default. The default is Arabic numerals.
whyOthersWrong.d: A period (.) is not a valid starting value for an ordered list in HTML. Starting values must be numbers for the default Arabic numeral type.

text:
Assertion (A): MOOC helps in providing education to dispersed students.
Reason (R): MOOC is a free web-based distance learning programme for large-scale interactive participation.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

explanation: Both statements are true: MOOCs (Massive Open Online Courses) do help dispersed students (A is true), and MOOCs are indeed web-based distance learning programs with large-scale participation (R is true). However, R does not explain WHY A is true — the reason MOOCs help dispersed students is because they are online and accessible anywhere, which is the nature of MOOC, not specifically that R explains A.

whyOthersWrong.a: While both A and R are true, R (describing MOOC as free web-based distance learning) does not serve as the direct/correct explanation for A (MOOC helping dispersed students). They are independent facts.
whyOthersWrong.c: R is not false — MOOCs are indeed web-based distance learning programmes designed for large-scale interactive participation.
whyOthersWrong.d: A is not false — MOOCs do indeed help in providing education to dispersed students who cannot attend traditional classrooms.

text:
Assertion (A):
is a container tag. Reason (R): HTML elements that have both an opening and a closing tag are known as container tags.

options.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true

text: The letter S in the abbreviation HTTPS in context of Networking protocols, stands for:
explanation: HTTPS stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure. The 'S' indicates that communication is encrypted using SSL/TLS, making it secure for transmitting sensitive data like passwords and payment information.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'Single' has no relevance to the HTTPS protocol. HTTPS refers to security/encryption, not singularity.
whyOthersWrong.b: 'Static' is not what HTTPS stands for. HTTPS is about security encryption, not static content.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Sensitive' is not the expansion. HTTPS uses 'Secure' to indicate SSL/TLS encryption protects the data being transferred.

text: Which of the following is NOT a Web Service?

options.d: Using a banking portal for online transaction

explanation: File transfer over Bluetooth is a local wireless technology (short-range, ~10m) that does not require the Internet. Web services are services accessed over the Internet/World Wide Web. Bluetooth transfers are not web-based.

whyOthersWrong.a: Diksha is a government e-learning portal accessed over the Internet — it is a web service (e-Learning).
whyOthersWrong.b: Sending and receiving email (via SMTP/POP/IMAP) is done over the Internet — it is a web service.
whyOthersWrong.d: Online banking portals are accessed through the Internet via a web browser — they are web services (e-Banking).

text: In 3G and 4G mobile technologies, the character 'G' stands for:
explanation: In mobile technology, 'G' stands for Generation. 3G = Third Generation, 4G = Fourth Generation, 5G = Fifth Generation. Each generation represents a new standard of wireless mobile communication with improved speed and capacity.

whyOthersWrong.b: GPRS (General Packet Radio Service) is a technology associated with 2.5G networks — it is not what 'G' stands for in 3G/4G.
whyOthersWrong.c: Grid has no relevance to mobile generations. 'Grid computing' is a separate technology concept.
whyOthersWrong.d: Google is a company, not a mobile technology standard. 'G' in 3G/4G refers to Generation of wireless networks.

text: A website or online platform where individuals or groups regularly publish written content, typically in a reverse chronological order is known as:
explanation: A Blog (short for Web Log) is an online platform where individuals or groups regularly publish written entries (posts) displayed in reverse chronological order (newest first). Examples: Blogger, WordPress.

whyOthersWrong.a: A News Group (Usenet newsgroup) is a discussion forum organised around a topic where users post and reply to messages — it is not primarily about individuals publishing content in reverse chronological order.
whyOthersWrong.c: A Chat Group is a real-time messaging space for multiple users. It is synchronous communication, not a publishing platform with reverse chronological posts.
whyOthersWrong.d: Social Networking sites (Facebook, Instagram) allow user profiles and social connections. While they include content publishing, the specific definition of 'reverse chronological personal publishing' best describes a Blog.

text: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of the <font> tag?
explanation: The <font> tag has three valid attributes: face (font typeface), size (1–7), and color (text color). 'height' is not an attribute of the <font> tag; height is used for elements like images, tables, and table rows.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'face' is a valid <font> attribute specifying the font family/typeface (e.g., <font face="Arial">).
whyOthersWrong.c: 'size' is a valid <font> attribute specifying the text size on a scale of 1–7 (e.g., <font size="4">).
whyOthersWrong.d: 'color' is a valid <font> attribute specifying the text color (e.g., <font color="blue">).

text: In HTML, we start a comment using:
explanation: HTML comments begin with <!-- and end with -->. Everything between these markers is ignored by the browser. Example: <!-- This is a comment -->

whyOthersWrong.b: '!-->' is the closing pattern of an HTML comment (-->), preceded by !, which is not correct for opening a comment.
whyOthersWrong.c: '--!>' is not valid HTML syntax for either opening or closing a comment.
whyOthersWrong.d: '<--!' reverses the correct syntax. The correct opening is '<!--', not '<--!'.

explanation:

whyOthersWrong.c: <hr> (horizontal rule) is an empty/void tag with no closing tag. It creates a horizontal line without content.
whyOthersWrong.d: (image) is an empty/void tag with no closing tag. It embeds an image using the src attribute.

text: The default color of vlink is ________.
explanation: In HTML, 'vlink' (visited link) is an attribute of the <body> tag that sets the color of links that have already been visited. The default color of visited links (vlink) is Purple. Unvisited links (link) default to Blue, and active links (alink) default to Red.

whyOthersWrong.a: Green is not the default color for any of the standard link states (link, vlink, alink).
whyOthersWrong.c: Blue is the default color of unvisited links (the 'link' attribute), not visited links (vlink).
whyOthersWrong.d: Yellow is not the default color for any standard link state in HTML.

text: Which of the following tags is NOT used while creating a description list?
explanation: <td> (Table Data) is a table cell tag used in HTML tables, not in description lists. A description list uses: <dl> (description list container), <dt> (description term), and <dd> (description definition/detail).

whyOthersWrong.a: <dt> (Description Term) is a required tag in description lists — it defines the term being described.
whyOthersWrong.b: <dl> (Description List) is the container tag that wraps the entire description list.
whyOthersWrong.d: <dd> (Description Definition) is a required tag in description lists — it provides the definition/description for the term in <dt>.

text: Which of the following is NOT an example of an Open Source Software?
explanation: Adobe Photoshop is proprietary (closed source) software — its source code is not publicly available and requires a paid licence. Linux, Android (AOSP), and OpenOffice are open source software with publicly available source code.

whyOthersWrong.a: Linux is a free and open source operating system kernel — its source code is publicly available under the GNU GPL licence.
whyOthersWrong.b: Android (AOSP — Android Open Source Project) is open source. The core Android OS code is available publicly, though Google's apps are proprietary.
whyOthersWrong.d: OpenOffice (Apache OpenOffice) is a free, open source office productivity suite — its source code is publicly available.

text:
Assertion (A): When you enter a query into a search engine, it retrieves and presents a list of web pages, documents, images, videos, or other types of content that are relevant to your search.
Reason (R): The goal of information retrieval is to effectively and efficiently find and present information that matches the user's search criteria.

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.c: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
options.d: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true

explanation: Both A and R are true. A correctly describes how a search engine works (retrieves relevant content for a query). R correctly states the goal of information retrieval (finding and presenting matching information). R directly explains WHY A is true — a search engine does this because its purpose is information retrieval as described in R.

whyOthersWrong.b: R IS the correct explanation of A. The reason a search engine retrieves relevant content (A) is precisely because the goal of information retrieval is to find and present matching information (R). R explains A.
whyOthersWrong.c: R is not false — the goal of information retrieval is indeed to effectively find and present information matching the user's search criteria.
whyOthersWrong.d: A is not false — search engines do retrieve and present relevant web pages, documents, images, and videos in response to a query.

text:
Assertion (A): It becomes difficult to update and maintain a website's design using CSS.
Reason (R): CSS allows web developers to separate the presentation layer (styles and layout) from the content layer (HTML).

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.c: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
options.d: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true

explanation: A is false: CSS actually makes it EASIER to update and maintain a website's design, not harder. One CSS file can style an entire website, so one change updates all pages. R is true: CSS does allow separation of presentation (styles) from content (HTML). Since A is false and R is true, option (d) is correct.

whyOthersWrong.a: A is false — CSS makes design maintenance EASIER, not difficult. Centralised styles mean one change updates the whole site.
whyOthersWrong.b: A is false — CSS simplifies website design maintenance significantly. It cannot be 'true' that CSS makes it difficult.
whyOthersWrong.c: A is false (not true) — CSS is specifically designed to ease design maintenance by separating presentation from content.

text: Arun is sending an e-mail to his office. Which protocol out of the following options will be used for the purpose?
explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is the protocol used for sending e-mails. It transfers emails from the sender's mail client to the mail server and between mail servers.

whyOthersWrong.a: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files between computers over a network, not for sending emails.
whyOthersWrong.b: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is used for transferring web pages between a web server and a browser, not for email.
whyOthersWrong.d: SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) is used to securely transfer files between hosts using SSH. It is not an email protocol.

text: Which of the following is NOT an e-Reservation portal in India?
explanation: Amazon.in is an e-Commerce/e-Shopping portal for buying goods online, not an e-Reservation portal. IRCTC, Yatra, and MakeMyTrip are travel and ticket reservation portals.

whyOthersWrong.b: Yatra.com is an online travel booking portal used to reserve flights, hotels, and holiday packages — it is an e-Reservation service.
whyOthersWrong.c: MakeMyTrip.com is an online travel booking portal for flight, hotel, bus and train reservations — it is an e-Reservation service.
whyOthersWrong.d: IRCTC (Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation) is the official government portal for online train ticket reservation — it is an e-Reservation service.

text: Which of the following attributes is NOT a valid attribute of the <font> tag in HTML?
explanation: The <font> tag has three valid attributes: face (font family), size (1–7), and color (text color). 'type' is not an attribute of <font>; 'type' is used with input, button, ol, and script elements.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'face' is a valid attribute of <font> specifying the font typeface/family (e.g., <font face="Arial">).
whyOthersWrong.c: 'size' is a valid attribute of <font> specifying the text size on a scale of 1 to 7 (e.g., <font size="3">).
whyOthersWrong.d: 'color' is a valid attribute of <font> specifying the text color (e.g., <font color="red">).

text: What is the full form of FTP?
explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol — it is a standard network protocol used to transfer files between a client and a server over the Internet or a TCP/IP network.

whyOthersWrong.b: 'File Transmission Protocol' is incorrect. The T in FTP stands for 'Transfer', not 'Transmission'.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'Fast Transfer Protocol' is incorrect. The F in FTP stands for 'File', not 'Fast'. FTP is not defined by speed but by its purpose.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'Fast Transmission Protocol' is doubly incorrect. F = File and T = Transfer, not Fast and Transmission.

text: Which of the following attributes is NOT a valid attribute of the <body> tag in HTML?
explanation: The <body> tag does not have a 'width' attribute. Valid <body> attributes include bgcolor (background color), background (background image), text (text color), link, vlink, alink, leftmargin, topmargin, etc. Width is used for elements like table, img, hr, etc.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'text' is a valid <body> attribute that sets the default text color of the entire web page (e.g., <body text="black">).
whyOthersWrong.b: 'background' is a valid <body> attribute that sets a background image for the web page (e.g., <body background="bg.jpg">).
whyOthersWrong.c: 'bgcolor' is a valid <body> attribute that sets the background color of the web page (e.g., <body bgcolor="yellow">).

text:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank:
A __________ is an online platform or website where individuals or businesses regularly publish articles/journals, known as posts, on various topics.
explanation: A Blog (Web Log) is an online platform where individuals or organizations regularly publish written content (posts/articles) on various topics, typically in reverse chronological order. Examples: Blogger, WordPress.

whyOthersWrong.a: A Browser (web browser) is software used to access and display web pages (e.g., Chrome, Firefox). It is not a platform for publishing content.
whyOthersWrong.c: A News Group (Usenet newsgroup) is a discussion forum on a specific topic where users post and reply to messages. It is not a platform for individuals publishing articles/journals as posts.
whyOthersWrong.d: A Web Server is hardware or software that stores and serves web pages to clients (browsers). It is infrastructure, not a content publishing platform.

text: The default value for the type attribute of an Unordered List in HTML is:
explanation: The default value of the type attribute of the <ul> (Unordered List) tag in HTML is 'disc' — a filled circle bullet point. Other valid values are 'circle' (hollow circle) and 'square'.

whyOthersWrong.a: 'circle' is a valid type value for <ul> (produces hollow circle bullets), but it is not the default. 'disc' is the default.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'square' is a valid type value for <ul> (produces square bullets), but it is not the default.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'triangle' is not a valid value for the type attribute of <ul> in standard HTML.

text: Which of the following is NOT a Search Engine available over the Internet?
explanation: Diksha (DIKSHA) is a national digital education platform launched by NCERT for school students and teachers. It is an e-Learning portal, not a search engine. Google, Bing, and Yahoo are search engines that index and retrieve web content.

whyOthersWrong.a: Google is the world's most popular search engine, used to search the web for any information.
whyOthersWrong.b: Bing is a search engine developed by Microsoft, an alternative to Google for web searches.
whyOthersWrong.d: Yahoo is one of the earliest and still active web search engines, also providing news and email services.

text: Which of the following options is a network protocol that enables secure and encrypted file transfers between a client and a server?
explanation: SFTP (Secure File Transfer Protocol) is a network protocol that provides file transfer capability over a secure (SSH-encrypted) connection. It protects data from interception during transfer.

whyOthersWrong.b: Telnet is a protocol for remote login to another computer, but it does not encrypt data — it transmits data in plain text, making it insecure.
whyOthersWrong.c: SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) also transfers files securely over SSH, but SFTP is more feature-rich and explicitly described as a 'file transfer protocol'. Both are secure, but the question's best match is SFTP.
whyOthersWrong.d: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is used for transferring web pages and is not encrypted. HTTPS is the secure version, but even that is for web content, not file transfers.

text: Which of the following options will set the font family of all paragraphs to 'Arial'?
explanation: The correct CSS property to set the font family is 'font-family'. The correct syntax is: p { font-family: Arial; } which applies the Arial font to all paragraph elements.

whyOthersWrong.b: 'fontfamily' (without the hyphen) is not a valid CSS property. CSS uses 'font-family' with a hyphen.
whyOthersWrong.c: 'font' is a CSS shorthand property that can set multiple font properties (style, variant, weight, size/line-height, family), but 'font: Arial' is not the correct shorthand syntax for just setting the family.
whyOthersWrong.d: 'font-type' is not a valid CSS property. The correct property name is 'font-family', not 'font-type'.

text:
Assertion (A): FTP is a networking protocol used for transferring files.
Reason (R): FTP is used when we want to view some data from a website.

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.c: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
options.d: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true

explanation: A is true: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is indeed used for transferring files between a client and server. R is false: Viewing data from a website uses HTTP/HTTPS, not FTP. FTP is for uploading/downloading files, not browsing web content.

whyOthersWrong.a: R is false — viewing website data uses HTTP, not FTP. So neither 'both true' options can be correct.
whyOthersWrong.b: R is false — FTP is not used to view website data. That is HTTP's purpose. So 'both true' is incorrect.
whyOthersWrong.d: A is true — FTP is genuinely a protocol for file transfers. It is not false.

text:
Assertion (A): SMS is an acronym for Smart Message Service.
Reason (R): SMS is the most common technology for delivering short, concise and important messages quickly.

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.c: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
options.d: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true

explanation: A is false: SMS stands for 'Short Message Service', not 'Smart Message Service'. R is true: SMS is indeed the most widely used technology for sending short text messages quickly and efficiently. Since A is false and R is true, option (d) is correct.

whyOthersWrong.a: A is false — SMS stands for Short Message Service, not Smart Message Service. So 'both true' cannot be correct.
whyOthersWrong.b: A is false — SMS is Short Message Service. So 'both true' is incorrect regardless of the explanation relationship.
whyOthersWrong.c: A is false (not true) AND R is true (not false). So this option has both parts wrong.

text: What is Internet?

options.b: A global network of interconnected computer networks
options.c: A local area network in a school

explanation: The Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks that uses the TCP/IP protocol suite to communicate. It connects millions of private, public, academic, business, and government networks worldwide.

whyOthersWrong.a: The Internet is not a type of software. Software like browsers and email clients use the Internet, but the Internet itself is a network infrastructure.
whyOthersWrong.c: A LAN (Local Area Network) in a school connects computers within a limited area. The Internet is global in scale and connects billions of devices worldwide.
whyOthersWrong.d: The Internet is not hardware. It is a network of networks, though it runs on physical hardware like routers, cables, and servers.

text: What is the primary purpose of the TCP/IP?

options.b: To store emails on the server
options.c: To define how data is transmitted over the Internet

explanation: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the fundamental communication protocol suite of the Internet. Its primary purpose is to define how data is transmitted, packaged, addressed, routed, and received over the Internet.

whyOthersWrong.a: Managing web pages is the role of HTTP/web servers, not TCP/IP. TCP/IP is a lower-level protocol for data transmission.
whyOthersWrong.b: Storing emails is the function of email servers using protocols like IMAP/POP3. TCP/IP handles the underlying data transmission, not email storage.
whyOthersWrong.d: Securing websites uses HTTPS (HTTP + SSL/TLS), not TCP/IP. TCP/IP itself does not provide encryption.

text: Which heading tag represents the smallest heading size in HTML?
explanation: <h6> represents the smallest heading in HTML. HTML provides 6 heading levels: <h1> (largest/most important) down to <h6> (smallest/least important).

whyOthersWrong.a: <h1> is the LARGEST heading in HTML, used for the most important heading on a page.
whyOthersWrong.b: <h3> is a medium-level heading — it is smaller than <h1> and <h2> but larger than <h4>, <h5>, and <h6>.
whyOthersWrong.c: <h5> is the second smallest heading, but <h6> is even smaller/lower priority.

text: In any email address, the username and the domain name are separated by _________ symbol.
explanation: The '@' (at) symbol separates the username from the domain name in an email address. For example, in 'student@school.edu', 'student' is the username and 'school.edu' is the domain name.

whyOthersWrong.a: '$' (dollar sign) is not used in standard email address syntax for separating username and domain.
whyOthersWrong.c: '#' (hash) is used in URLs for fragment identifiers and in programming, but not as a separator in email addresses.
whyOthersWrong.d: '%' (percent) is used in URL encoding for special characters, but not as a separator in email addresses.

text: Which of the following refers to the rules that enable computers to communicate over a network?
explanation: A Protocol is a set of rules and standards that govern how data is transmitted and received over a network, enabling computers to communicate with each other. Examples: TCP/IP, HTTP, SMTP, FTP.

whyOthersWrong.a: A Browser (web browser) is software for accessing and displaying websites. It uses protocols to communicate, but it is not itself the set of rules.
whyOthersWrong.b: e-Banking is an internet service for conducting banking transactions online. It is not the rules that enable network communication.
whyOthersWrong.d: A Text Editor is software for editing plain text. It has no role in defining network communication rules.

text: In the POP3 protocol, what does the number '3' signify?

options.c: It refers to three main servers used in email delivery
options.d: It indicates the third version of the Post Office Protocol

explanation: POP3 stands for Post Office Protocol version 3. The '3' indicates that it is the third and current version of the POP email retrieval protocol. It is used to download emails from a mail server to a local client.

whyOthersWrong.a: The '3' does not refer to three computers. POP3 is a version number, not a count of computers.
whyOthersWrong.b: The '3' does not stand for the year 2003. It is a version number that has been in use since the 1980s.
whyOthersWrong.c: The '3' has nothing to do with three servers. It is simply the version number of the protocol.

text: Which of the following is NOT a valid type of list in HTML?
explanation: HTML has three standard list types: Ordered List (<ol>), Unordered List (<ul>), and Description List (<dl>). 'Detail list' does not exist as a standard HTML list type.

whyOthersWrong.a: Description list (<dl>) is a valid HTML list type that pairs terms (<dt>) with their descriptions (<dd>).
whyOthersWrong.b: Ordered list (<ol>) is a valid HTML list type that displays items in a numbered/lettered sequence.
whyOthersWrong.d: Unordered list (<ul>) is a valid HTML list type that displays items with bullet points.

text: Ajay, a computer engineer, generally uses his laptop to remotely access customers' computers in order to diagnose problems in their computer. Which protocol is being used for this purpose?
explanation: TELNET (Telecommunication Network) is a protocol that allows a user to remotely log in to and control another computer over a network. Ajay is using TELNET to remotely access customers' computers for diagnosis.

whyOthersWrong.a: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files between computers, not for remote login/access and diagnostics.
whyOthersWrong.b: SMS (Short Message Service) is for sending text messages over mobile networks, not for remote computer access.
whyOthersWrong.c: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending emails. It has no functionality for remote computer access.

text: What is World Wide Web?
explanation: The World Wide Web (WWW) is a system of interlinked hypertext documents and multimedia content accessed via the Internet using a web browser. It was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

whyOthersWrong.a: The World Wide Web is not hardware. It is an information system of web pages accessible over the Internet.
whyOthersWrong.b: The WWW is not software for managing data. It is a system of documents linked via hyperlinks and accessed through browsers.
whyOthersWrong.d: A Web server is a computer/software that stores and serves web pages. The WWW is the system of all those pages, not just one server.

text: What is the purpose of the start attribute in the <ol> tag?

options.a: To change the type of bullets
options.b: To specify the total number of items in the list
options.c: To create a list within another list
options.d: To set the starting number of the list

explanation: The 'start' attribute in the <ol> tag sets the starting number for the ordered list. For example, <ol start="5"> will begin numbering from 5 instead of the default 1.

whyOthersWrong.a: Changing the type of bullets/numbering style is done using the 'type' attribute of <ol>, not 'start'. For example, type="a" for alphabetical.
whyOthersWrong.b: The 'start' attribute does not specify the total number of items. Items are simply added as <li> elements; their count is not a property of the list.
whyOthersWrong.c: Creating a list within another list (nested list) is done by placing an <ol> or <ul> inside a <li>, not through the 'start' attribute.

text:
Assertion (A): Blogs are an effective way for individuals to share their thoughts, knowledge, and experiences online.
Reason (R): Only professional web developers can create and maintain blogs.

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.c: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
options.d: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true

explanation: A is true: Blogs are indeed an effective way to share thoughts and experiences online. R is false: Anyone can create and maintain a blog using platforms like Blogger, WordPress, or Medium — no professional coding skills are required.

whyOthersWrong.a: R is false — blogs are accessible to everyone, not just professional developers. Platforms like WordPress make blogging easy for anyone.
whyOthersWrong.b: R is false — it is incorrect that only professionals can create blogs. This option requires R to be true.
whyOthersWrong.d: A is true — blogs are genuinely effective for sharing content online. This option requires A to be false.

text: Assertion (A): The tag will display an image even if the src attribute is not specified. Reason (R): The src attribute provides the path to the image file, which is essential for the browser to locate and display the image.

options.a: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.b: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
options.c: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
options.d: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true

explanation: A is false: Without the src attribute, the tag cannot display any image — the browser has no path to find the image file. R is true: The src attribute is essential as it provides the file path that the browser uses to locate and render the image. Since A is false and R is true, option (d) is correct.

whyOthersWrong.a: A is false — cannot display an image without src. And if R explains A, A must be true, which it is not.
whyOthersWrong.b: A is false — without src displays nothing (or a broken image icon). Both A and R cannot both be true.
whyOthersWrong.c: A is false (not true) — without src, no image is displayed. R is true, not false.
